alignments.note: Verb with its subject pronoun and auxiliary (rule 17).

Construct noun rendered *door posts* with a supplied *the*, no article morpheme present (rule 29). Head moved to *door*: *posts* alone is any post, and the ASV never writes a bare *posts* for מְזוּזָה, so it is the supplied generic and *door* carries the lexeme — rule 31's own תִּמֹרָה → *palm trees* is the precedent. Heading on *posts* as the English compound's noun was the competing reading.
Nomen rectum takes the relational *of* (rule 19); discontinuous around the possessive (rule 25).

review_notes: Head of the מְזוּזֹת unit moved from *posts* to *door* under rule 31: the subtraction test leaves *posts* naming any post, and the tie-break — whether the ASV ever writes that class noun alone for the word — is not met, מְזוּזָה being rendered *door-posts* or *side-posts* throughout. Rule 31's listed תִּמֹרָה → *palm trees* is the direct precedent.
Edges are unchanged: the supplied *the* stays on the construct under rule 29 and the *of* on the rectum under rule 19.
